_comment: ADR-037 register fragment — consumer-secrets-writeonly (ocon#147 phase B, openregister#380). SECURITY FIX. The sibling `source` fix (99-source-secrets-writeonly.json) was never applied to `consumer`, so `authorizationConfiguration` — which holds a consumer's inbound `apiKey`, or its `publicKey`/`algorithm` for the JWT issuer path — was still returned in CLEARTEXT by the generic OpenRegister object API. That is not a theoretical path: ConsumersController is a placeholder with no read endpoint of its own, so the consumers tab reads these objects straight from `/apps/openregister/api/objects/openconnector/consumer` — the leaking path IS the UI path, and every MCP tool over the same schema inherits it. `writeOnly: true` makes OpenRegister's render boundary (or#386) strip the field from EVERY API response — admin included, body and `@self.relations` index copy alike. A field the server never returns cannot leak, whoever reads it. The engine is unaffected and was verified, not assumed: BOTH consumer readers already resolve in system context — AuthorizationService::findIssuer() and ::resolveConsumerByApiKey() each pass `_rbac: false`, and writeOnly stripping is gated on `_rbac === true`, so inbound apiKey matching and JWT issuer validation keep working untouched. NotificatiesSubscriberService::provisionConsumer() only WRITES the apiKey (and sends its own local copy to the remote), never reads it back, so it is unaffected too. Marked on `authorizationConfiguration` only — `authorizationType`, `domains`, `ips` and the rate/quota blocks are non-secret operational config the UI legitimately renders.
